drug.proposed_mechanism: Fully human IgG1 monoclonal antibody that binds to EGFR and antagonizes binding of its cognate ligands, blocks ligand-induced phosphorylation of EGFR and downstream signaling, inhibits EGFR-dependent tumor cell proliferation, and targets EGFR-expressing tumor cells for killing through antibody-dependent cell cytotoxicity (ADCC)
drug.intended_biology: Inhibition of EGFR signaling pathway to suppress tumor growth and survival

trials.indication: Stage IV squamous non-small cell lung cancer
trials.target_population: Previously untreated patients with histologically or cytologically confirmed squamous NSCLC, Stage IV disease, age ≥18 years, ECOG PS 0-2, adequate organ function
trials.effect_size: HR 0.84 (95% CI 0.74, 0.96), median OS 11.5 months vs 9.9 months (1.6 month improvement)
trials.target_engagement_evidence: Population PK analysis showed necitumumab average concentration at steady state of 216 μg/mL resulted in increase in survival time of approximately 48 days relative to control
biomarker_changes: EGFR protein expression analysis showed 95.2% of patients had tumors expressing EGFR, but H-score cutoff of 200 was not predictive of efficacy outcomes
subgroup_findings: Treatment effect consistent across subgroups except patients ≥70 years (HR 1.03, 95% CI 0.75-1.42)
Patients with 0% EGFR expression appeared not to benefit
trials.dose_information: Necitumumab 800 mg IV on days 1 and 8 of 3-week cycle, gemcitabine 1250 mg/m2 on days 1 and 8, cisplatin 75 mg/m2 on day 1
trials.duration: Treatment until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity; median follow-up not specified
trials.outcome_summary: The addition of necitumumab to gemcitabine/cisplatin resulted in statistically significant 1.6-month improvement in median OS and 0.2-month improvement in PFS, but with increased toxicity including fatal sudden deaths and thromboembolic events.
trials.reviewer_commentary: The reviewer concludes that the results of the SQUIRE trial support a positive benefit:risk assessment of necitumumab and recommends its approval in combination with gemcitabine and cisplatin for first-line treatment of patients with metastatic squamous NSCLC. While the safety issues are of concern, the overall incidence and severity are consistent with other anti-EGFR monoclonal antibodies currently on the market.

trials.indication: Stage IV non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer
trials.target_population: Previously untreated patients with histologically or cytologically confirmed non-squamous NSCLC, Stage IV disease, age ≥18 years, ECOG PS 0-2, adequate organ function
trials.effect_size: HR 1.01 (95% CI 0.84, 1.21), no improvement in median OS
safety_signals: Study closed prematurely due to imbalance in deaths and thromboembolic events
trials.dose_information: Necitumumab 800 mg IV on days 1 and 8 of 3-week cycle, pemetrexed 500 mg/m2 on day 1, cisplatin 75 mg/m2 on day 1
trials.duration: Study closed prematurely after enrolling 633 of planned 947 patients
trials.outcome_summary: The study was closed prematurely due to an imbalance in deaths and thromboembolic events in the necitumumab arm, with no efficacy benefit observed in non-squamous NSCLC.
trials.reviewer_commentary: The reviewer notes that the lack of efficacy in the INSPIRE trial demonstrates that necitumumab is not effective in non-squamous NSCLC and recommends adding a Limitation of Use statement that PORTRAZZA is not indicated for treatment of non-squamous NSCLC.

trials.target_population: Patients with histologically-confirmed solid tumors who no longer responded to standard therapy or for whom no standard therapy was available, age ≥18 years, ECOG PS 0-2
trials.primary_endpoint: Safety profile and maximum tolerated dose
trials.effect_size: MTD established at 800 mg for both weekly and every-2-week schedules
trials.target_engagement_evidence: At doses of 600 mg weekly or 800 mg every other week, geometric mean trough concentrations were above 40 μg/mL (target associated with antitumor activity in preclinical models)
safety_signals: DLTs at 1000 mg every 2 weeks: grade 3 headache, nausea, vomiting
trials.dose_information: Escalating doses from 100-1000 mg, weekly (Arm A) or every 2 weeks (Arm B) in 6-week cycles
trials.outcome_summary: First-in-human study established 800 mg as the MTD and recommended dose, with safety profile consistent with anti-EGFR antibodies and preliminary antitumor activity observed.
trials.reviewer_commentary: The reviewer notes this study established the appropriate dose and schedule for necitumumab, with toxicities consistent with other anti-EGFR monoclonal antibodies.

trials.target_population: Japanese patients with advanced solid tumors not responsive to standard therapy, age ≥20 years, ECOG PS 0-1, adequate organ function
trials.effect_size: No DLTs observed, MTD not reached at maximum planned doses
trials.target_engagement_evidence: All 3 regimens generated trough concentrations above 40 μg/mL throughout the study
safety_signals: Most common AEs: headache (66.7%), dry skin (66.7%), pruritus (53.3%), rash (53.3%)
trials.dose_information: 600 mg or 800 mg IV on days 1 and 8 every 3 weeks, or 800 mg every 2 weeks
trials.duration: 14 of 15 patients completed Cycle 1, 9 patients received at least 1 dose in Cycle 2 or beyond
trials.outcome_summary: Japanese dose-finding study confirmed that necitumumab can be safely administered to Japanese patients at the same dose regimen as Western patients.
trials.reviewer_commentary: The reviewer notes that based on PK and safety data, necitumumab can be safely administered to Japanese patients at the same dose regimen recommended for Western patients.

trials.indication: Locally advanced or metastatic colorectal cancer
trials.target_population: Treatment-naive patients with histologically confirmed EGFR-detectable or undetectable colorectal adenocarcinoma, age ≥18 years, ECOG PS ≤2
trials.effect_size: ORR 64% (95% CI 47.8, 77.6%), median OS 22.5 months, median PFS 10 months
safety_signals: Most common grade ≥3: neutropenia (29.5%), asthenia (27.3%), rash (20.5%)
4 deaths within 30 days of last dose
trials.dose_information: Necitumumab 800 mg, oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2, folinic acid 400 mg/m2, 5-FU 400 mg/m2 bolus + 2400 mg/m2 46-hour infusion every 2 weeks
trials.outcome_summary: Single-arm study in colorectal cancer showed promising activity with 64% response rate, but with significant toxicity including 4 deaths within 30 days of treatment.
